I will keep this year simple and steady. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will rely mainly on the pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits my local weather, my water conditions, and the work rhythm I know well. I do not want to spread myself too thin with too many crops, because at my age I care more about stable output and manageable labor than chasing a risky high return. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps standability and yield, but I will not make the plan complicated. For the wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, a topdressing of nitrogen, a few irrigations at key stages, and limited pesticide sprays only when pressure is real. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly to catch moisture and heat, use more nitrogen on the maize than on the wheat, and keep tillage lighter so I can save labor and keep the season moving. I will also keep a small peanut field in spring to spread risk a little and give myself some cash income, but I will not make peanuts my main crop because wheat and maize are still the safest backbone for me here.
